newsitem.title: RWANDA: Rwanda, Zaire in heavy fighting overnight.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda, Zaire in heavy fighting overnight.

text.p: The Rwandan army said on Tuesday it exchanged eight hours of heavy gunfire with Zairean government forces across the border town of Bukavu overnight.
Emmanuel Ndahiro, Rwanda's defence ministry spokesman, told Reuters that Zairean forces in Bukavu opened fire first using anti-aircraft guns and 75 mm rifles.
It was the second night of fighting between the two sides each firing from their own territory around the Zairean border town of Bukavu.

Zaire's relations with Rwanda have worsened recently but have been poor since 1994. More than one million Rwandan Hutu refugees live in camps in eastern Zaire from where Rwanda says they mount guerrilla incursions.
The Hutus fled their homeland fearing reprisals for the genocide in 1994 of up to one million minority Tutsis and pro-opposition Hutus in Rwanda.
"There was more fighting last night. We are checking for casualties. The truth is that they (Zaireans) fired first. We opened fire in response," Ndahiro said.
The U.N. refugee agency said it was considering the evacuation of some staff from Bukavu.

"There is a plan to evacuate non-essential expatriate staff from Bukavu. We have sent recommendations to New York (U.N. headquarters) and we are awaiting a response," Fernando del Mundo, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said by telephone from Geneva.
Brenda Barton, a spokeswoman for the U.N. World Food Programme (WFP) in the Kenyan capital Nairobi, said the agency was also awaiting orders from headquarters.
"We are considering the relocation of non-essential staff from Bukavu. They (staff) will be relocated to Nairobi," said Barton.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) said it would continue to operate there despite the fighting.
"Operations are continuing in Bukavu, Uvira and Cyangugu," said Bernhard Julier, head of the ICRC in Rwanda. "We are not suspending or evacuating any of our operations."
The International Federation of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) pulled out three of its seven foreign staff in Bukavu on Monday.
IFRC official Jon Valfells said indiscriminate shelling began late on Sunday.
"Two shells fell in the garden of the Bukavu hotel where most foreign aid workers stay," he said.

The firing followed the Zairean government stepping up its campaign against neighbours Rwanda and Burundi and aid agencies by accusing them of promoting or aiding armed Tutsi infiltrators on missions to destabilise its volatile eastern refugee zone.
Zaire government spokesman Oscar Lugendo said on Saturday Rwanda sent Tutsi infiltrators of the Banyamulenge group, most of whom have lived in eastern Zaire for generations.
The government warned aid agencies caring for the estimated 1.1 million Rwandan Hutu refugees in camps in eastern Zaire that they would be banned unless they limited themselves to aid work.
Human rights watchdog Amnesty International on Friday accused Zairean troops and officials of atrocities against Banyamulenge civilians in eastern Zaire over the past month.
There are some 400,000 Banyamulenge, all of whom claim to be Zairean.
